newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban advises civilians to quit warzone.
newsitem.headline: Taleban advises civilians to quit warzone.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban government told civilians on Tuesday to leave frontline areas north of the capital Kabul to avoid harm and reported that its fighters had repulsed attacks in the northern province of Baghlan.

A broadcast by the official Kabul radio, monitored in Islamabad, quoted a governent statement as saying the purist Islamic militia intended to carry out a large-scale operation against its opponents in Kapisa province and around the towns of Golbahar and Jabal os-Siraj.
It said government forces beat back a three-ponged attack in Baghlan province, where a Taleban force is besieged at the strategic town of Pul-i-Khumri.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report.
The opposition's fighters struck from the province of Samangan in the north, Doshi district in the south and Kayan valley in the southwest, the broadcast said.
"Tens of militiamen were killed and wounded, some were arrested and some weapons and ammunition were seized," Taleban said.

Forces of opposition guerrilla commander Ahmad Shah Masood took Golbahar, on the mouth of his native Panjsher Valley, and Jabal os-Siraj, on the main highway from Kabul to the north, late last month after the Taleban forces were ousted by local militias from the newly-taken northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif.
The Taleban said at the weekend that it had recaptured Jabal os-Siraj but other Afghan sources said Masood's forces still controlled the town.
The Taleban government's statement on Tuesday said experience of the past nine months had shown that Masood's forces had used homes of local residents as positions to fight the Taleban.

"The government has always wanted not to increase bloodshed and harm people," it said. "Therefore, it requests you to vacate the areas to let the Taleban carry out a large-scale operation to root out the (opposition) militias."
